paragraphs: Spout sells software that sends utility notifications by text, email, voice, and mail. The site says the platform supports boil water notices, water main breaks, planned or unplanned outages, water quality issues, pressure problems, and weather-related advisories. Targeting is by service area, street, zip code, or custom group, so only affected customers receive an alert.

Leak detection runs off the meter reading system, where smart meters flag continuous flow patterns that indicate a potential leak. Notifications then go to customers automatically or manually, across more than one channel. Leak status and resolution can be tracked across the whole customer base.

Spout connects to a utility's existing AMI, billing system, and customer portal, and the integration is done on the vendor side. Most utilities are up and running within a few weeks, according to the site.

quote.text: Most utilities start with one use case, like leak notifications or service disruption alerts, and expand from there.
